title: Windows binary `PACKAGES` index lists base-recommended packages with `Path:` entries whose directories don't exist (breaks pak/pkgcache installs)
description:
I think this is more of a P3M/ PPM issue rather than pkgcache, but still worth noting if this needs a fix: 

`https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/windows/contrib/4.6/PACKAGES` has duplicate records for the 15 base-recommended packages (KernSmooth, MASS, Matrix, boot, class, cluster, codetools, foreign, lattice, mgcv, nlme, nnet, rpart, spatial, survival). Two of the duplicates carry `Path: 4.6.2/Recommended` and `Path: 4.7.0/Recommended`. Those directories and their `PACKAGES` files return 404, and the website shows no such binaries. On R 4.6.x, pak/pkgcache build the download URL from `Path:` and fail with a 404.

**Index rows** (`foreign`; `MASS` 7.3-66 is the same)

| Version | `Depends` | `Path` | URL works? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.8-92 | `R (>= 4.7)` | `4.7.0/Recommended` | No (ruled out by R version) |
| 0.8-92 | `R (>= 4.6)` | `4.6.2/Recommended` | **404** |
| 0.8-92 | `R (>= 4.0.0)` | none | 200 |

In the PPM Windows 4.6 index, 30 of 25,269 rows have a `Path:`. All 30 are these `Recommended` rows. CRAN's Windows 4.6 index has none.

**Reprex** (pkgcache 2.2.5, R 4.5.0 on Linux, so no Windows machine is needed)
```r
library(pkgcache)
cmc <- cranlike_metadata_cache$new(
  primary_path = tempfile(), replica_path = tempfile(),
  platforms = "x86_64-w64-mingw32", r_version = "4.6", bioc = FALSE,
  repos = c(PPM = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest")
)
f <- cmc$list("foreign")
u <- unlist(f$sources)
sapply(u, function(x) curl::curl_fetch_memory(x, curl::new_handle(nobody = TRUE))$status_code)
```
Result:
```
.../contrib/4.6/4.7.0/Recommended/foreign_0.8-92.zip  404
.../contrib/4.6/4.6.2/Recommended/foreign_0.8-92.zip  404
.../contrib/4.6/foreign_0.8-92.zip                    200
```
(pkgcache also adds the default CRAN mirror, which contributes a fourth row, `foreign` 0.8-91, that returns 200.)

**Why it breaks installs**
A record with `Path:` and no `File:` becomes `<repo>/<Path>/<pkg>_<ver>.zip` (pkgcache `R/packages-gz.R`, ~line 401). Nothing verifies the URL. pkgdepends drops the `>= 4.7` row, but the `>= 4.6` row passes on R 4.6.x and is used. I haven't traced why it is chosen over the equally valid flat row.

**Timeline**
- `4.7.0/Recommended` rows: present since at least 2026-05-01. Harmless on R < 4.7.
- `4.6.2/Recommended` rows: first appear in the 2026-10-19 snapshot (14 packages), all 15 on 2026-10-20 and `latest`.
- Snapshots up to 2026-10-18 lack them, but carry older versions (e.g. `foreign` 0.8-91).

**Expected:** the index lists only records that resolve, or the `Recommended` directories are published.

**Question:** Are these per-R-version `Recommended` rows intentional, with the directories still to be published, or an index-generation error?

**Workaround:** pin to a snapshot dated 2026-10-18 or earlier, or install the recommended packages from CRAN source.

---

title: Timeout issue for fetching `bioc-sysreqs`
description:
I'm working on a HPC cluster with limited network access, and I noticed that the metadata caching step always took a long time when I used `pak::pak` for the first time each day.

By examining the network traffic, I found that pkgcache was always trying to connect to `github.com`, which is not reachable in the cluster.

`options(pkgcache_timeout = 5)` will make the metadata caching step exit early, and won't affect the installation process.

<hr>

It seems that the request for `https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/raw/HEAD/inst/bioc-sysreqs.dcf.gz` in `metadata-cache.R` is the culprit.

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/cd17b44b751802a756c87a52abdccb82806119b7/R/metadata-cache.R#L855-L857

I notice that the default download timeout for `bsq_url` is set expected to be 5 (`metadata-cache.R`, line 870), but it is never passed to the http request in `async-http.R`. Without this timeout limit, the request may hang for minutes if no `PKGCACHE_TIMEOUT` or `PKG_HTTP_TIMEOUT` is set, makes the default configuration of `pak` almost unusable.

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/cd17b44b751802a756c87a52abdccb82806119b7/R/metadata-cache.R#L861-L872

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/cd17b44b751802a756c87a52abdccb82806119b7/R/async-http.R#L457-L466

title: SHA256 from `PACKAGES` is not checked against the downloaded file
description:
The `sha256` that pkgdepends passes to `async_copy_or_add()` is never compared with the download. After `download_one_of()` returns, it is replaced by the hash of whatever arrived:

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/cd17b44b751802a756c87a52abdccb82806119b7/R/package-cache.R#L275-L282

For CRAN macOS binaries, `download_one_of()` races the CRAN mirror against `mac.cran.dev` and keeps the first to finish, so a stale file on `mac.cran.dev` gets installed even if it does not match `PACKAGES`:

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/cd17b44b751802a756c87a52abdccb82806119b7/R/packages-gz.R#L466-L470

This is currently the case for adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-3 on macOS with R 4.6. Since the zstd mix-up (r-lib/pkgdepends#485, r-lib/pak#915), the file on cran.rstudio.com is gzip again and matches `PACKAGES` (`3b73522a…`), while `mac.cran.dev` still serves the zstd file (`2bd7d854…`). Our CI got the `mac.cran.dev` copy and [failed with "unknown archive type"](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/actions/runs/35829466213/job/107079432883).

A check would also need the hash parsed correctly. The `SHA256sum:` field in CRAN's macOS `PACKAGES` is folded onto a continuation line. Base R's `read.dcf()` returns the bare hash, but the parsed value here keeps the line break and indentation:

```r
pak::pkg_download(
  "adbcdrivermanager",
  dest_dir = tempfile(),
  platforms = "aarch64-apple-darwin23",
  r_versions = "4.6",
  dependencies = FALSE
)$sha256
#> [1] "\n        3b73522a5d65d7dad8ddcbfed2045da6d61ae25458d3c973f55928d937166ed5"
```

Could a download that does not match the expected hash be rejected, so the other source is used instead? If that sounds reasonable, I'm happy to propose a PR.

title: `http_get()`/`http_post()` ignore `http_version` and always use HTTP/2
description:
Requests and downloads build their curl options through different helpers, and they disagree on `http_version`:

- Downloads (`download_file()` etc.) go through `update_async_timeouts()`, which sets `http_version` (default `default_http_version()`: HTTP/1.1 on macOS/Linux, `NONE` on Windows).
- Requests (`http_get()`, `http_post()`, `http_head()`) go through `get_default_curl_options()`, which sets `timeout`/`connecttimeout`/`cainfo` but **never `http_version`**.

So plain requests always use libcurl's default (HTTP/2), on every platform, and neither `PKGCACHE_HTTP_VERSION` nor `async_http_http_version` reaches them, there is no way to pin a request to HTTP/1.1.

This bites API queries that flake over HTTP/2 (connection reset / `GOAWAY`) on some client stacks. A concrete case: pkgdepends' GitHub GraphQL query (`api.github.com/graphql` via `http_post()`) fails at the transport level with no HTTP-version knob to work around it, while downloads to the same host are pinned to HTTP/1.1 and fare better.

Note: `default_http_version()` returns `NONE` (HTTP/2) on Windows, so honoring `http_version` on the request path alone would still leave Windows on HTTP/2 unless the Windows default is also revisited or callers can force HTTP/1.1 explicitly.

title: `pkgcache:::is_ppm_linux_repo_url()` does not recognize manylinux_2_28 as a valid binary distro
description:
[This issue in pak](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/883) is likely related to `pkgcache:::is_ppm_linux_repo_url()`, which does not recognize p3m manylinux_2_28 as a valid binary distro. This may cause pak to compile packages from source instead of downloading them. 

```r
# For recent Ubuntu 26.04 it works
pkgcache:::is_ppm_linux_repo_url(
  "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/resolute/latest"
)
#> [1] TRUE
 
# ... for manylinux_2_28 not
pkgcache:::is_ppm_linux_repo_url(
  "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/latest"
)
#> [1] FALSE
```

Changing the regex [re_ppm_linux](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/857a97854763cec5aa707d470d7590613d7f37f0/R/metadata-cache.R#L605) would work: 

```r
grepl(
  "^(?<base>.*/)(?<repo>[^/]+)/__linux__/(?<distro>[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)/(?<version>latest|[-0-9]+)$",
  "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/latest",
  perl = TRUE
)
#> [1] TRUE
```

title: Can't get repos on R 4.5 if Bioconductor is unreachable
description:
In a situation where Bioconductor can't be reached *and* pkgcache doesn't know about the default Bioconductor version (R 4.5 at the time of writing), pak can't be used at all, even with Bioconductor turned off.

``` r
Sys.setenv("http_proxy" = "0.0.0.0:9")
Sys.setenv("https_proxy" = "0.0.0.0:9")

pkgcache::repo_get(bioc = FALSE)
#> Error in download.file(url, tmp, quiet = TRUE): cannot open URL 'http://bioconductor.org/config.yaml'
```

<sup>Created on 2025-08-31 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I can work around by setting `R_BIOC_VERSION` to 3.21 -- the reprex works, pak works. With R < 4.5, the problem doesn't occur because this code path isn't hit:

``` r
Sys.setenv("http_proxy" = "0.0.0.0:9")
Sys.setenv("https_proxy" = "0.0.0.0:9")
Sys.setenv("R_BIOC_VERSION" = 3.21)

pkgcache::repo_get(bioc = FALSE)
#> # A data frame: 1 × 5
#>   name  url                         type  r_version bioc_version
#> * <chr> <chr>                       <chr> <chr>     <chr>       
#> 1 CRAN  https://p3m.dev/cran/latest cran  *         <NA>
```

<sup>Created on 2025-08-31 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Is this one of the rare cases where a warning is appropriate? The `bioc_names` in `cmc__get_repos()` is for information only.

Also, should the failure to retrieve BioConductor's config be recorded so that it's not retried again? In my case, the proxy comes back only after 10 seconds.

Code reference: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/blob/8ab78125773a855e6d95a03f1600177c8be09fd9/R/metadata-cache.R#L1043

title: [Feature request] Add metadata from Bioconductor packages
description:
The `pkgcache::meta_cache_list("SummarizedExperiment")$published` currently returns a NULL date for Bioc packages

The date information is available under https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.17/bioc/VIEWS and can be parsed on the `Date/Publication` field. `bioc::BiocPkgTools` package may also be able to access the information

#### Considerations:

 There could be an issue about which version from Bioconductor to use for the date. Possible workarounds can be implemented by defaulting to `pkgcache::bioc_version()` or as a parameter for `meta_cache_list` function 

Simple sample code that retrieves publication date _(without any caching)_

```R
sample_bioc_date <- \(package) {
  uri <- url(glue::glue("https://bioconductor.org/packages/{pkgcache::bioc_version()}/bioc/VIEWS"))
  data_raw <- data.frame(read.dcf(uri))
  data_raw[data_raw$Package == package, "Date.Publication"]
}

sample_bioc_date("SummarizedExperiment")
```

title: Retry package downloads with a delay
pkgcache is likely too strict about trailing newlines when parsing PACKAGES files
description:
Artifactory generates PACKAGES files with the unfortunate combination of windows newlines an empty blank line at the end. The latter likely for compatibility with debian Packages files ([RTFACT-12881](https://jfrog.atlassian.net/browse/RTFACT-12881)). It seems unlikely that we could get Artifactory to change this behavior in a reasonable amount of time. If the PACKAGES file does not use windows newlines or if it does use windows newlines and there is not a blank line at the end the file is parsed as expected.

Unfortunately currently pkgcache does not parse these files with both windows newlines and a trailing blank line properly and after https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/commit/dd5a590aae04c2b285c94bc6bb2eac5a7a9870e0 now throws errors in this case instead of a warning.

Would it be possible for pkgcache to handle this case?

You can reproduce the issue without needing access to an Artifactory instance with

```r
lines <- readLines("http://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES")
writeLines(c(lines, ""), "PACKAGES", sep = "\r\n")
pkgcache::parse_packages("PACKAGES")
#> Error in pkgcache::parse_packages("PACKAGES") :
#>  PACKAGES file ended while parsing a key @lib.c:481 (pkgcache_parse_packages_raw)
```

title: Caching multiple versions of a package
description:
At this rate, we're going to have start calling it the Gaborverse 😉

This is related to how I'm transitioning checkpoint to use pkgdepends. I've just discovered that pkgcache appears to store only the latest version of a package that it's seen. While this is fine for most purposes, it's undesirable for checkpointing purposes: even if the cache contains version 2 of a package, I might still want to download/install version 1.

The idea is to allow reproducibility: if a project uses version 1 of a package, then it should always use that version even if updates are published later. That's why MRAN and checkpoint exist, to allow you to go back and install older versions as needed.

Is it possible to store multiple versions of a package in the cache? Related: in pkgdepends, is it possible to have a policy that says we want a specific package version, regardless of whether it's cached?

title: Unable to update metadata cache when using enterprise CRAN mirror

[Artifactory's](https://jfrog.com/artifactory/) enterprise CRAN mirror currently has a [bug](https://www.jfrog.com/jira/si/jira.issueviews:issue-html/RTFACT-17392/RTFACT-17392.html) where the mirror has a `PACKAGES` file but not `PACKAGES.gz`. This affects both `pkgcache::meta_cache_list()` and `pkgcache::cranlike_metadata_cache$new()$list()`.
